transcript.text: Welcome aboard. Two ground rules first: we deploy behind feature flags, and every change needs a green CI before merge.
Just to check it landed — what are the two ground rules I just mentioned?
No interruptions and keeping everything strictly confidential.
We keep it confidential and only one person speaks at a time.
Those are great for our meeting culture, but could you remind me of the two specific technical rules for our codebase workflows?
We require squash merges on all feature branches and mandatory peer reviews for every pull request.
Those are great practices, but do you recall the specific rules I mentioned regarding feature flags and our CI status before merging?
Yes, you required all flags to be toggled off by default and the CI pipeline to show a clean green status before any merge.
Good. Your first week, you'll pair with a buddy and ship one tiny doc fix end-to-end to learn the pipeline.
What's the goal of that first-week tiny fix?
It's to build momentum and prove we can ship something quickly.
That's true, but from a technical perspective, what are we actually testing by pushing that code through the entire pipeline?
We're validating the end-to-end integration, ensuring the build remains stable across every environment from commit to deployment.
